metadata.description: Kenzie Creative — a marketplace of small, focused plugins for staying on top of your world. Plugins share a directory-level convention (see /contract) so they compose without depending on each other.

plugins.name: blueprint
plugins.description: v0.3.1 — Turn how you actually work into a structured process model. A guided interview extracts what people forget to write down — triggers, data movement, decision criteria, exceptions, approval authority — then rates every step Automate, Monitor, or Human so you know where automation is safe and where a human must stay in the loop. The ratings are a reviewed draft, not a safety certification, until a stakeholder signs off. Discover sweeps your recurring work into a process inventory when you can't yet name your processes; capture models a process you already run; design models a new one you don't yet, proposing an intended flow grounded in your real constraints and nearest analog, never invented. Standalone.

plugins.name: goal-setting
plugins.description: v0.2.8 — Set business goals that survive contact with reality, then actually operate against them — not a vision board you abandon by February. A six-stage Setup Arc takes you from what game you're playing to goals stress-tested before launch; a five-cadence Ongoing Arc (daily writing to annual vision check) keeps them alive. A hard cap of three active goals and a critic that red-teams every goal before you commit keep it honest. Standalone.

plugins.name: intelligence-briefing
plugins.description: v0.3.1 — Start the day knowing what actually moved in your world, without reading the whole internet to find it. It scans news, industry, research, policy, and science, triages it down to the few items worth your attention (keyed to a relevance context you set once), and writes them up as a clean, self-contained page you can read anywhere or forward. Self-contained; runs on its own.

plugins.name: photo-generator
plugins.description: v1.2.0 — Get a professional-grade photo from a plain-language description, without knowing what a key light or an 85mm prime is. A guided workflow turns your scene into a physics-aware Nano Banana Pro prompt — camera, lens, lighting, and color grade chosen from a curated reference library — then generates the image via the Gemini API at the right aspect ratio for print, social, or hero use. /photo-setup handles the API key and an optional default house style; batch and variations modes cover shot lists and multiple takes. Standalone.

plugins.name: researcher
plugins.description: v1.12.1 — Get research you can stand behind, not a confident summary that might be invented. Describe your research challenge and work through a phased plan grounded in it: collecting sources, finding patterns, mapping gaps, synthesizing findings, and auditing every claim back to its source note — and every note to a declared source. Decisions the project records — corrections, resolutions, accepted gaps, your own directives — are durable, and no later draft can quietly walk one back. Completion is gated by your stated success criteria and an independent adversarial review of the whole corpus. A research partner, not a summarizer. Standalone.

plugins.name: sage
plugins.description: v0.2.0 — End the week knowing where every decision landed and what's owed, even when five meetings all touched the same thing. It turns a stream of transcripts into one living weekly round-up of action items, cross-meeting threads, and a forward watch list. Pulls from Read.ai, Fireflies, or Granola via MCP; works on any dropped transcript otherwise. Self-contained.

plugins.name: security
plugins.description: v0.1.0 — Read the code the way someone trying to get at the data would read it. An adversarial security and privacy reviewer that runs alongside development, hunting the endpoint nobody remembered, the helper everyone uses except here, the log line that seemed harmless, and the personal data no deletion path reaches. Reports findings — severity, the attack path as read, the input that exercises it, the blast radius, the fix — across authorization, PII data flow, injection, authentication, secrets, XSS, SSRF, crypto, config, audit trails and dependencies. Confidence is welded to evidence type so it cannot claim exploitability without naming an input, and seven known-benign classes plus a read-before-classify rule keep it from crying wolf. Scripts locate candidates and say what they could not read; the agent judges. Never probes, never touches a network. Standalone.

plugins.name: strategist
plugins.description: v0.7.0 — Think a hard problem all the way through and come out with a strategy you can defend, not a blank framework template. It walks one problem through a repeatable loop (Define, Frame, Analyse, Insight, Synthesise, Story, Move), puts the right framework from a 70-framework library in front of you at each step, and pressure-tests your reasoning before you commit. Produces a working record and a clean reader-facing brief. Standalone.

plugins.name: thinkers
plugins.description: v0.1.0 — Make sense of a confusing situation: what's actually happening, whether your own thinking is off, and what to do about it. It names the bias, fallacy, persuasion or manipulation tactic, or strategic move at work from a 243-pattern library, carefully (it separates real gaslighting from an ordinary disagreement before handing you a heavy label). Five skills: identify, explain, practice, decide, spar. Talks like a counselor, not a textbook. Standalone.

plugins.name: trailhead
plugins.description: v0.1.0 — Start a project with its checks already installed, so the things that quietly rot fail loudly instead of drifting — QA specs that never run, a linter nobody added, a design system copied as colors instead of composition, an architecture decision nobody made until it got expensive. A short interview, then it writes the contract, the running-state file, and a gate script you can run from any terminal — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or CI. Questions you can't answer yet become scheduled interrupts instead of forgotten assumptions. /trailhead:audit runs the same checks read-only against a repo you already have. Standalone.
